newsitem.title: CHINA: China's stock indices end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: China's stock indices end up on speculative buying.

text.p: China's B share indices closed higher on Monday in line with the A share markets on speculative demand, brokers said.
Shanghai's B share index rose 0.517 points or 0.82 percent to 63.354 points and Shenzhen's B index gained 2.07 points or 1.44 percent to end at 145.23.
Meanwhile, Shanghai's A share index rose 1.48 percent or 14.2 points to close at 974.146 points, and Shenzhen's A index advanced 4.54 points or 1.31 percent to close at 351.17 points.
"The rise in the A share market was linked to strong gains in index-weighted counters," a Shenzhen-based broker said. "But trading remained speculative."

On the Shanghai B share market, institutional support for selective stocks was active in order to attract fresh capital, but follow-up buying was limited on uncertainties over firms results, brokers said.

"The talk that a meeting about B shares and H shares (China companies listed in Hong Kong) will be held this week sparked some speculative institutional buying," one Shanghai broker said. "It is expected to give positive news."
Shanghai Steel Tube was the star on speculative buying, rising $0.010 or 5.88 percent to $0.180. Market giant Shanghai Tyre followed, rising $0.020 or 4.90 percent to $0.428.

Tientsin Marine Shipping was the most active share on speculative buying sparked by the talk that it would offer bonus shares, ending up $0.022 or 4.84 percent to $0.476 on volume of 2.8 million shares.
On the Shenzhen B share market, investors were seen cautiously building up positions in shares likely to report strong results, brokers said.
Conglomerate Lionda put in the strongest performance with a rise of HK$0.30 or 8.22 percent to HK$3.95 on speculative buying.
Hotelier Dadonghai, the most active issue, edged up HK$0.05 to HK$3.70 after 1.06 million shares were traded.

On Shanghai's A market, Guojia was the star on news that the company would develop real estate project with a Singapore firm, jumping 0.58 yuan or 10 percent to its limit-up of 6.55 yuan on volume of 325,900 shares.
In Shenzhen, power supplier Zhuhai Huadian A share closed at its 10 percent limit-up at 4.90 yuan due to speculative buying, brokers said.
